verdict: Yes, the price engine will run at full size on Thursday. On a made-up cache of F1's real shape (4,841 calls, 24.6 million outcome rows read, 4.25 million two-sided quotes kept), `uv run markets price-engine` finished in 2 min 47 s and used at most 7.6 GB of memory. Memory and time grew roughly in step with the number of calls, and no step grew faster. A heavier stress version that also lists every FCS game (5,231 calls, 7.7 million quotes) finished in 5 min 36 s at 12.3 GB. No patch is needed and none was written. Thursday needs about 8 GB of free memory (up to about 12.5 GB), under 10 minutes, and under 1 GB of disk for the F1 cache and the engine's outputs. The 32 GB laptop can do this as long as nothing else large is running at the same time. This afternoon, for comparison, orphaned workers held about 90 GB of memory and pushed swap to 74 GB.

**Disk.**

| Item | Size |

**What the made-up cache contains.**
- **Calls:** 4,841, planned by the real bulk.plan_calls from real 2020 to 2025 kickoff times: 1,790 NFL and 3,051 CFB. 234 of them are sealed 2026 calls, made up by moving 2025 kickoffs forward 52 weeks; no 2026 data was read. This matches the runbook's 5,407, which includes the whole 2026 season.
- **Games per snapshot:** a snapshot lists every game from 3.5 hours before it (in-play) to 21 days after it. That averages 39 NFL games (maximum 59) and 141 CFB games (maximum 259).
- **Books and markets:** ten books and three markets. About 8% of books skip a whole game and 3% of markets are missing.
- **Prices:** lines drift and retail books go stale. 0.68% of retail sides have an expected value of 2% or more.
- **Kickoffs:** 5% of kickoffs move by 1 to 4 hours and 0.5% of games are postponed.
- **Duplicates:** the 10-minute snapshot grid before September 2022 produced no duplicate snapshots.

defects.title: Machine-health risk for Thursday: orphaned workers can use up memory, and swap uses up disk
defects.evidence: At 16:45 on Sep 29, top showed about 90 GB of memory footprint in orphaned Python workers: runbook_margins.py (PID 99923, whose parent was launchd, 6 workers at about 11 GB each) and false_stops.py (PID 17772, 6 workers at about 4.4 GB each), both run from scratchpad/rev63r4 with the wf_4a9a6642-bf1-2 worktree's venv. `sysctl vm.swapusage` showed 74 GB used of 74.7 GB. Free space on /System/Volumes/Data was 11 GB and then 9.7 GB a few minutes later, because macOS swap files sit on that disk. By 16:52 the workers were gone, swap was down to 7 GB and 74 GB of disk was free. The hub was told by message at the time. The engine itself is fine (7.6 GB peak).
defects.smallest_fix: Just before `uv run markets price-engine` on Thursday, check three things: `top -l 1 -o mem -n 8` shows no leftover multi-GB Python workers, `df -h /System/Volumes/Data` shows at least 10 GB free, and `vm_stat` shows at least 12 GB free or inactive. Run nothing else heavy alongside the engine.

defects.title: The Gemini audit's size projection (A12) is wrong
defects.evidence: The report says: under 1 minute and about 600 MB for an 8.1M-row load. Measured on F1's real call plan: 24.6 M outcome rows are read, not 8.1 M, because every snapshot lists games outside the 7-day window. Loading alone takes 134 s, the whole run takes 167 s, and peak memory is 7.6 GB, about 12 times the projection. This agrees with the hub's note that the auditor's own log (450 calls, 38 s, 866 MB) contradicts the projection. The hub's extrapolation of 10 GB or more was close.
defects.smallest_fix: None to the code. Do not rely on A12. Use the measurements here.

for_the_amendment: nothing. No code change is needed, so there is no patch and nothing for the amendment. Every run finished well under 16 GB and 30 minutes. If the hub wants a record, one line would do: "A full-size run on a made-up cache of F1's shape was measured on Sep 29, 2026 at about 3 minutes and 7.6 GB, and a stress version with FCS games at about 6 minutes and 12.3 GB. No change was made."
could_not_check: There is no real Odds API featured response on this Mac, so the made-up bodies follow the documented format and the engine's fixture. Real JSON has no spaces between items, which makes it a little smaller; real prices may compress a little worse. The disk estimate of 0.2 to 0.6 GB is a range for that reason.

How far ahead a real featured snapshot lists games is unknown. I listed games up to 21 days out plus in-play games, as the brief asked. A longer real horizon adds loading time (about 5.4 microseconds per outcome row) but barely changes peak memory, because rows more than 9 days out are dropped as each batch is read.
Whether the real NCAAF feed lists FCS-only games is unknown. The stress run with every FCS-involved game (12.3 GB, 336 s) is the upper bound I tested.
The made-up cache over-counts books: all ten books quote every season, but Fanatics and ESPN BET did not exist before late 2023. So there are more quotes than real, which errs toward a heavier test.

Duplicate snapshots (two calls returning the same snapshot) did not occur in the made-up data. A few are possible on the real 10-minute grid before September 2022. The duplicates step ran at 5.2 GB, below the final peak, but a large number of duplicates was not tested.

Bowl games for 2020 to 2022 are made up by copying 2023's (the processed table stops before them), so 127 made-up games have no score. The sealed 2026 calls are 2025's schedule moved 52 weeks; no 2026 table row, price or result was looked at.
Memory was measured as maximum resident size. Compressed memory was not measured, but the Mac had free memory during every measured run, so the two should be close.

Outside interference. My first full-size attempt at 16:58 was killed from outside at startup (exit 137). At 17:01 a second copy of my own full-size command started from the same Claude process without my asking; I stopped it after 37 s. Another agent also wrote data/, scripts/ and games_meta.parquet into this same scratch folder. I left those untouched, but I emptied scratch tmp/ at 17:14, when no process from that folder was running. The measured 100% run agrees with a later clean rerun: outputs byte-identical, time within 1 s.
The CFB team_info files were symlinked read-only into the worktree so name matching ran as it will in the live checkout. The links were removed afterwards and the worktree is clean at 4bf0497.
